title: 2024 AMC 8 Problem 17
statement: A chess king is said to attack all the squares one step away from it, horizontally, vertically, or diagonally. For instance, a king on the center square of a \(3 \times 3\) grid attacks all \(8\) other squares, as shown below. Suppose a white king and a black king are placed on different squares of a \(3 \times 3\) grid so that they do not attack each other. In how many ways can this be done?

solutions.text:
Count ordered placements by first choosing the square for the white king. If the white king is in the center, it attacks every other square, so there are \(0\) choices for the black king.

If the white king is in a corner, it attacks \(3\) squares, so the black king has \(9-1-3=5\) safe squares. There are \(4\) corner choices, giving \(4\cdot5=20\) placements.

If the white king is on an edge but not a corner, it attacks \(5\) squares, so the black king has \(9-1-5=3\) safe squares. There are \(4\) such edge choices, giving \(4\cdot3=12\) placements.

The total number of placements is \(20+12=32\).

Thus, E is the correct answer.
hints: Count ordered placements for the white king first
A corner allows \(5\) safe black-king squares; an edge-center allows \(3\)
